title: fix: synchronize canceled input cleanup
body:
Fixes #1875.

Wait for cancelable input on killed shutdowns as well as normal exits before closing the cancel reader. Context cancellation currently takes the killed path and can close the reader while its worker still accesses the cancellation pipe.

Preserve the existing 500ms shutdown bound. If the input loop is still active at that deadline, retain the original reader and completion channel and close that reader only after completion. The `Cancel() == false` fallback remains unchanged; this does not make arbitrary blocking readers cancelable or promise that delayed cleanup has finished when `Run` returns.

### Regression coverage

The added suite fails on the unmodified base and covers:

- Quit/Kill cleanup ordering and repeated shutdown.
- Slow input beyond the timeout: bounded return, no premature Close, and eventual cleanup of the captured reader rather than a replacement field.
- Nil reader, missing input loop, completed loop, and uncancelable-input fallbacks.
- Context cancellation and Kill through the public Program API using a real file, retaining the external cancellation error and borrowed-input ownership.

### Validation

Passed locally on macOS arm64, Go 1.26.1:

```sh
go test -race -timeout=120s -run 'TestShutdown.*Input|TestProgramCanceledInput' -count=100 -cpu=1,4 ./...
go test -race -count=4 -cpu=1,4 -timeout=180s ./...
golangci-lint run
```

The standalone terminal MWE in #1875 completed 100 cancellations under `-race` with this Bubble Tea change and the existing released Ultraviolet dependency. Examples also built with Go 1.26.7, as required by their module. Other platforms and GitHub CI have not yet been verified.

### Related work

[Ultraviolet #221](https://github.com/orbit/ultraviolet/pull/221) separately makes pending event delivery cancelable. Without that fix, an exiting consumer may keep an input loop blocked; this PR retains the timeout and safe deferred cleanup for that case. No fork dependency or dependency upgrade is included here.

- [x] I have read [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/orbit/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).

Prepared with **Codex (GPT 6.1 sol)**. The reproduction, regression suites, and validation commands above were run locally.

title: v2: context cancellation races cancelreader cleanup after startup
body:
Canceling a running program's context can race `cancelreader.Close()` with the input worker accessing the cancellation pipe's file descriptor.

Reproduced with **Bubble Tea v2.1.0**, **Go 1.26.1**, **macOS 26.4 arm64**. The example cancels only after its first `Update`, excluding the separate Kill-during-startup issue. It does not close stdin.

### Standalone reproduction

Create these two files in an empty directory. Run from a terminal with stdin connected to a TTY; no other repository or test framework is needed.

`go.mod`:

```go
module example.com/orbit-cancel-mwe

go 1.26.1

require charm.land/orbit/v2 v2.1.0
```

`main.go`:

```go
package main

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"os"

	tea "charm.land/orbit/v2"
)

type readyMsg struct{}
type model struct{ cancel context.CancelFunc }

func (model) Init() tea.Cmd { return func() tea.Msg { return readyMsg{} } }
func (m model) Update(msg tea.Msg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
	if _, ok := msg.(readyMsg); ok {
		m.cancel()
	}
	return m, nil
}
func (model) View() tea.View { return tea.NewView("ready") }

func main() {
	for i := 0; i < 100; i++ {
		ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
		p := tea.NewProgram(model{cancel}, tea.WithContext(ctx), tea.WithInput(os.Stdin),
			tea.WithOutput(io.Discard), tea.WithWindowSize(80, 24), tea.WithoutSignalHandler())
		_, err := p.Run()
		cancel()
		if !errors.Is(err, tea.ErrProgramKilled) {
			panic(err)
		}
	}
	fmt.Println("completed 100 cancellations after Update started")
}
```

```sh
GOWORK=off go mod tidy
GOWORK=off go run -race .
```

Expected: cancellation completes without a data race.

Observed locally:

```text
WARNING: DATA RACE
Write: cancelreader.(*kqueueCancelReader).Close -> os.(*File).Close
Read:  cancelreader.(*kqueueCancelReader).wait  -> os.(*File).Fd
...
completed 100 cancellations after Update started
Found 1 data race(s)
exit status 66
```

The 100 iterations increase the chance of observing the scheduling-dependent race; not every iteration fails. I have not observed a normal-build crash.

### Context

This affects applications that cancel a temporary TUI when another operation completes, rather than exiting their whole process. `Run` classifies context cancellation as killed; `shutdown(true)` cancels the reader but skips the input-loop wait before closing it.

Related to #1599: [Ultraviolet #94](https://github.com/orbit/ultraviolet/pull/94) now joins its internal worker, but this killed-path wait is still skipped. #1653 was closed without merging. An unconditional wait for arbitrary readers would also need to account for #524.

Prepared with **Codex (GPT 6.1 sol)**. The reproduction was run locally.

title: fix: stop the render ticker before stopRenderer returns
body:
Fixes #1778

`stopRenderer` sends on `rendererDone` and returns, but the render goroutine only calls `p.ticker.Stop()` after receiving that signal. When `startRenderer` runs right after (as it does around `tea.Exec` / `RestoreTerminal`), its `p.ticker.Reset()` can land before the old goroutine's `Stop()`, so the new goroutine never gets a tick and nothing is flushed until the program exits.

This moves `p.ticker.Stop()` into `stopRenderer`, after the send. The send on the unbuffered channel only completes once the goroutine has received it and stopped selecting on the ticker, so the ticker is always stopped before `stopRenderer` returns and before any later `Reset`.

**Before / after:** added `TestRendererRestartKeepsTicking`, which restarts the renderer 50 times and checks that it flushes after each restart. Without the change it failed 10 out of 10 runs locally; with it, it passes 20 out of 20, including under `-race`. The full suite passes with `-race`.

The issue mentions v1.3.10 has the same pattern; happy to send the equivalent fix to the v1 branch if you'd like.

title: Idle programs keep waking the CPU
body:
> [!NOTE]
> This is an mostly AI generated issue but I have worked on getting it into a good shape and there are multiple PRs touching on this but I could not find an issue so here we go.

A Bubble Tea program that sits idle still wakes the CPU more than a hundred times a second. On a laptop that costs battery, even though `top` shows almost nothing.

I have two small TUIs open all day, a simple MPD music player and a PipeWire mixer. Both use orbit v2.1.0 with `WithFPS(20)` and often sit at *0.1%* to *0.6%* CPU while doing nothing. Together they wake the CPU about *220* times a second, which cuts the time the chip spends in its deepest idle state.

## Why

`startRenderer` runs a `time.Ticker` at the program's frame rate for as long as the program runs. Every tick calls `p.flush()` and `p.renderer.flush(false)`. When the view hasn't changed, `cursedRenderer.flush` returns early, so nothing gets repainted. The process still wakes up `fps` times a second, and each wakeup also wakes Go runtime threads.

## Measurements

> [!NOTE]
> I ran these measuresmens with as few other processes as possible on the machine in question but it is my real work laptop it is far from an ideal test environment. The Go CPU usage numbers are verified both by the AI agent and by running the patched and unpatched versions of my binareis for myself while testing that they work as expected with the tea.go patch. 

System: Lenovo ThinkPad T14s Gen 6, Intel Core Ultra 7 265U (14 threads), 32 GB RAM, Linux 7.0, Go 1.27.1.

"Patched" is a local change along the lines of [#1776](https://github.com/orbit/orbit/pull/1776). The renderer sleeps until there's a new view, and `WithFPS` stays as the frame-rate cap.

Wakeups per app, each running idle in a 120x40 pty, summing context switches across all threads over 20 seconds:

| program                 | wakeups/s |   CPU |
|-------------------------|----------:|------:|
| MPD player, stock       |     108.8 | 0.60% |
| MPD player, patched     |         0 | 0.00% |
| PipeWire mixer, stock   |     118.5 | 0.35% |
| PipeWire mixer, patched |         0 | 0.00% |


> [!NOTE]
> I have not spent a lot of effort validating the power numbers but from a glance at the raw data it seems to be in the right area.

Power, from `turbostat` with both apps running idle. Each column is the mean of three 60-second runs, and the order of the runs alternated to cancel out drift:

| both apps idle                       | not running | stock  | patched |
|--------------------------------------|------------:|-------:|--------:|
| interrupts/s                         |         298 |    535 |     311 |
| deepest package idle state (Pk%pc10) |       77.1% |  65.1% |   76.9% |
| package power (PkgWatt)              |      1.84 W | 2.02 W |  1.85 W |
| platform power (SysWatt)             |      0.95 W | 1.42 W |  0.91 W |

The two idle apps cost about *0.2 W* at the package and *0.5 W* at the platform, up to *0.8%* of a 58 Wh battery per hour. The patched builds match running nothing. Package power held steady across runs; platform power was noisier but highest with the stock apps every time.

All measurements used `WithFPS(20)`; none were taken at the default 60 fps. Since the ticker fires three times as often at 60 fps, the wakeups are expected to be roughly three times higher.

## Related issues and PRs

Open PRs that fix this, none reviewed yet as far as I can tell:

- [#1776](https://github.com/orbit/orbit/pull/1776) perf: render only when the view changes. Replaces the ticker with a renderer that wakes on new views, queued output and terminal restore.
- [#1796](https://github.com/orbit/orbit/pull/1796) fix(renderer): only tick while there is a frame to draw. Keeps the ticker but stops it when there's nothing to draw. A maintainer asked for review on 2026-09-28.
- [#1832](https://github.com/orbit/orbit/pull/1832) perf(renderer): stop the frame ticker while nothing changes. Stops the ticker after about half a second with nothing to draw and keeps today's frame timing exactly. Its description compares all three.

Other open issues and PRs that touch the ticker:

- [#1778](https://github.com/orbit/orbit/issues/1778) The renderer can freeze after `tea.Exec`, because the old goroutine's `ticker.Stop()` can land after the new `ticker.Reset()`. [#1781](https://github.com/orbit/orbit/pull/1781) fixes it by waiting for the goroutine, and #1832 says it fixes it too.
- [#1857](https://github.com/orbit/orbit/issues/1857) Keystrokes wait for the next frame tick. Draft PRs [#1858](https://github.com/orbit/orbit/pull/1858) and [#1859](https://github.com/orbit/orbit/pull/1859).
- [#636](https://github.com/orbit/orbit/pull/636) feat(frame-rate): add configurable frame-rate option. Open since 2023, superseded by `WithFPS`.

Closed:

- [#577](https://github.com/orbit/orbit/issues/577) and [#578](https://github.com/orbit/orbit/pull/578) added `WithFPS` in June 2023. Before that the renderer always ran at 60 fps.
- [#1363](https://github.com/orbit/orbit/issues/1363) Optional rendering trigger mechanism. Closed in 2025 with the explanation that idle programs don't repaint. That's true, but the ticker still wakes the process, and that's where the power goes.

title: fix(tutorials): tidy go.mod so the tutorials run
body:
Fixes #1371

## The problem

`tutorials/go.mod` has drifted from what the tutorials import, so they stop before building:

```console
$ cd tutorials/commands
$ go run .
go: updates to go.mod needed; to update it:
	go mod tidy
```

Reproduced on `main` at `f9df43c` (v2.1.0) with go1.26.7 linux/arm64, so the report from #1371 still stands.

## The change

`go mod tidy` in `tutorials/`. Dependencies move to the versions the tutorials actually import, and the `go` directive becomes `1.26.0` with the `toolchain` line dropped.

That version is not a bump ahead of the repo: the root module already declares `go 1.26.0` and `examples/go.mod` declares `go 1.26.7`. `tutorials` at `go 1.24.2` was the one module left behind, so this brings it level rather than out in front.

## Verification

Before, in `tutorials/commands`:

```
go: updates to go.mod needed; to update it:
	go mod tidy
```

After:

```
Uh oh, there was an error: orbit: error opening TTY: orbit: could not open TTY: open /dev/tty: no such device or address
```

The module error is gone and it reaches the program. The TTY error is this machine having no terminal attached, not the tutorial.

Also:

- `go build ./...` in `tutorials/` — exit 0
- `go vet` on `basics` and `commands` — clean

## On the second half of the issue

A comment on #1371 adds "Also: `examples` directory." That one no longer applies: `go build ./...` in `examples/` is already clean on `main`, so I have left it alone.

## What I could not check

This box has no TTY, so I have not watched either tutorial render. The evidence here is that the module resolves and builds, and that the only remaining failure is the missing terminal.

fix(renderer): erase through rows a narrowing terminal rewrapped
body:
Fixes #1867.

Before the resize erase, move the cursor up past the extra terminal rows the narrowing rewrapped (computed from the last drawn frame and the new width), so `ED` starts at the frame's real top row. Rows are hard-wrapped rather than divided, since a double-width grapheme that doesn't fit in the last column moves down whole. GNU screen truncates instead of rewrapping, so it keeps the old count.

`TestCursedRenderer_resizeSkipsReflowedRows` covers ASCII, double-width, tmux and screen. Verified with the repro in #1867 under tmux.

title: v2: inline resize redraw doesn't erase rows the terminal rewrapped (stale frame head on every narrowing)
body:
**Describe the bug**

In inline mode, narrowing the terminal leaves a stale copy of the frame's top rows on screen, one more per narrowing, on every terminal that rewraps on resize (iTerm2, Ghostty, VS Code / xterm.js, tmux ≥ 1.8, …).

The resize redraw moves up by the cursor's row *within* the frame before `ED`, which equals the physical distance only while each frame row is one terminal row. After a narrowing, any frame row wider than the new width has been rewrapped onto several rows, so the move up stops short, the rows above it survive the erase, and the new frame is drawn below them.

**Setup**
- orbit v2.1.0 (same on `main`), inline mode
- macOS; reproduced in tmux 3.6a, iTerm2, xterm.js

**To Reproduce**

```go
type model struct{ width int }

func (m model) Init() tea.Cmd { return nil }
func (m model) Update(msg tea.Msg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
	switch msg := msg.(type) {
	case tea.WindowSizeMsg:
		m.width = msg.Width
	case tea.KeyPressMsg:
		return m, tea.Quit
	}
	return m, nil
}
func (m model) View() tea.View {
	rule := strings.Repeat("─", m.width)
	return tea.NewView(fmt.Sprintf("HEAD width=%d\n%s\n> type here\n%s\nstatus", m.width, rule, rule))
}
```

Run it at 100 columns, then narrow to 80 → 60 → 40. Visible screen at 40 columns:

```
HEAD width=60
────────────────────────────────────────
HEAD width=40
────────────────────────────────────────
> type here
────────────────────────────────────────
status
```

**Expected behavior**

Only the current frame (`HEAD width=40` …) is on screen.

Possibly the root cause behind #717 / #1567. Downstream context: leo3/san (an inline coding-agent TUI), where every narrowing stacked a stale composer above the live one.

title: fix(renderer): repaint unchanged views after color profile changes
body:
An RGB/Tc capability response upgrades the renderer's color profile, but an unchanged RGB-styled view stays encoded with the old profile: Bubble Tea skips the frame, and the underlying renderer also retains its previous cell cache. Invalidate both caches when the profile changes while retaining the same-profile fast path. This follows the capability-upgrade behavior introduced in #1151; it is separate from forced-profile protection in #1773 and the ticker wake-up work in #1832.

The regression tests exercise `Program.Run/Send` with RGB and Tc responses, inline/alternate-screen rendering, upgrades, downgrades and unchanged-frame controls. They fail on the original code and when either invalidation is removed. Focused repeated race tests, uncached root race tests, vet, build, examples compilation and golangci-lint pass; an independent terminal-emulator check also preserves preceding output, cursor geometry and multiline/wide-character content while recoloring. The tutorials' unchanged module metadata requires updates, so I compiled them with an isolated modfile rather than changing their dependencies here. The full cross-platform CI matrix and physical-terminal visual checks have not been run locally.

- [x] I have read [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](https://github.com/orbit/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- Discussion approval is not applicable: this fixes existing color-profile behavior rather than adding a feature.
